channel.title: The Western Producer - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Western Producer (producer.com)

item.title: Lower seeding rate favours mustard composite
item.description: A three-year study found composite mustard AAC Yellow 80 responds better to nitrogen than the open-pollinated Andante variety and yields higher.

item.title: Auctioneer champion returns to the big leagues
item.description: Brennin Jack, branch manager of Heartland Livestock Services in Virden, is headed to the 2026 World Livestock Auctioneering Championship.

item.title: Saskatchewan map maker helps put history on the wall
item.description: Pronghorn Maps is located in Alex McPhee’s house. There, he prints maps of all kinds — election maps, historical farm maps, Hutterite colony maps, the list goes on.

item.title: Grazing lease controversy in southern Alberta municipality reaching critical juncture
item.description: A southern Alberta rural municipality continues its years long process of balancing the needs of native grassland preservation and economic development on its tax-recovery lands.

item.title: Wadena family-owned dealership celebrates 60 years in business
item.description: Finding a family owned, single-store dealership is increasingly rare. But, the Sowa family in Wadena, Sask., say they have no plans to change their multi-brand, single-store business model.

item.title: Marit in Washington at agriculture policy conference
item.description: Saskatchewan’s agriculture minister is in Washington this week to highlight how essential agricultural trade is to both countries.

item.title: Weak loonie expected to help agriculture exports in 2026
item.description: FCC said the weak Canadian dollar should help keep ag exports strong in 2026 as Canada continues to diversify away from the U.S.

item.title: Wind chill is important but confusing
item.description: The measurement called wind chill accounts for air temperature, wind speed and the presence of moisture in the air. It was first introduced in 1939 by explorer Paul Siple.

item.title: VIDEO: Fewer words are better when working with dogs
item.description: An Alberta dog trainer believes that body language, posture and hand signals are much more important that verbal commands.

item.title: Pest Management Regulatory Agency denies strychnine emergency use request
item.description: Emergency use of strychnine for the 2026 growing season has been denied by the Pest Management Regulatory Agency.
